summary: Linguist Werner Abraham studied at TU Wien, the University of Innsbruck, and the University of Vienna (PhD ~1965). He held posts at Illinois, Tübingen, and Munich, and was appointed professor of German linguistics and medieval studies at Groningen in 1971.

Werner Sundermann was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Derek F. Maher, attended East Carolina University, and studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA from International Christian University and a PhD from Harvard (~1975). He served at the University of Illinois (~1976–1978) and UC Davis (~1978–2005).

Indologist and religious studies scholar Whitney Cox studied at the University of Virginia and University of Chicago, working under Sheldon Pollock and others. Cox held posts at SOAS (~2007–2013) and became a professor at the University of Chicago (~2013).

Scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne studied at the University of Ceylon (BA 1952) and University of London (PhD ~1956). He taught at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973) and served as professor and dean at Kelaniya.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Colorado Boulder and Stanford University, studying under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Religious studies scholar Wilfred Cantwell Smith studied at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton (PhD ~1948). He held posts at Forman Christian College, McGill University, Dalhousie, and Harvard, where he directed the Center for the Study of World Religions (~1964–1973).

Philosopher Wilfrid Sellars studied at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the universities of Iowa (~1938–1946), Minnesota (~1947–1958), and Yale (~1958–1963), before serving as a professor at the University of Pittsburgh from 1963 to 1989.

Wilhelm Deecke, who worked in linguistics and Indology, earned a doctorate from Leipzig and studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as director of the Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Bouxwiller, and Lycée Albert-Schweitzer Mulhouse.

Philosopher Wilhelm Dilthey studied at Heidelberg and the University of Berlin. He held academic positions at the universities of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel (~1868–1871), Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Geiger was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he became professor in 1891, later serving as professor at Munich (1920–1924).

Wilhelm Gesenius worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Helmstedt (~1803–1806) and Göttingen (~1806), where he also held a post (~1806–1810) before serving at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1810–1842).

Sinologist and linguist Wilhelm Grube studied at Saint Petersburg and Leipzig (PhD 1880) under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Georg von der Gabelentz. He worked at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1884; 1892).
Wilhelm Gundert was a scholar in Japanology and religious studies. He succeeded Karl Florenz and held an academic post at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1936 to 1945.

Wilhelm Halbfass, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at Vienna and Göttingen (Promotion ~1967). He held a post at Göttingen (~1968–1970) and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from 1982 to 2000.
Linguist and Indologist Wilhelm Havers held academic appointments at the universities of Bern (~1913–1915), Leipzig (~1915–1920), Würzburg (~1920–1929), Breslau (~1929–1937), and Vienna (~1937–1953).

Wilhelm K. Essler, active in philosophy and Indology, studied at the University of Munich under Wolfgang Stegmüller and Wilhelm Britzelmayr (~1960–1966). He served as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1980–2005).

Wilhelm Max Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1883–1885) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1885–1888), and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania from around 1902 to 1919.

Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. Beginning in 1855, he held librarian posts at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha, becoming its director in 1883, and led Schloss Friedenstein from 1874.
